description:
FINDING (2026-11-13, measured on the probe distinct1.fz, base 4247853cd): the saving is real but the shape below cannot be built without a behaviour change.
Repeat rate: 2,320 times a reader's dependency edges were removed and later re-installed for the same reader; 1,750 (75%) re-installed exactly the same set; 12,615 of 12,647 removed edges (99.7%) came back.
Why 'install only added, remove only dropped' does not apply: the removal is not at the re-install. At unblock 0 of 2,281 calls had a previous pending record, and at commit 29 of 5,197 did. The edges are dropped earlier, in displace_for_reproduction_shallow and reject_group, so a displaced reader has no edges during the gap. Keeping them through the gap would make mutate_product_wave walk displaced readers (dirty_descendants.insert on a product neither produced nor pending), which changes validation.
Reserving dependency maps from the previous run's count: prototyped, no change in allocation calls (1,017,956 both ways), about 5 KB fewer bytes. Not worth building.
What a real fix needs: a design decision, e.g. remembering a displaced reader's last edges (new state) or changing when displacement drops edges (behaviour). Neither is authorised by this ticket. Needs a proposal before any build.

ORIGINAL: ProductSessions install_reader_dependencies (pull.rs:1194/1201, from unblock :1133 and commit :1050): each wait-and-rerun cycle removes the reader from every dependency's reader set, dropping a set that empties (pull.rs:1213-1229), and the re-run installs the same edges into fresh HashSets. About 15k allocations, 8 MB. Also pull.rs:2308 and :2353: each position product's dependency maps grow from empty for the usual two to four reads (about 20k, 7 MB). Do not change what any table is keyed by (fz-xcu).
title: A re-run keeps the reader edges it still has
